QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_28

question.text: A Category II debt AIF invests in a mezzanine note to a mid-market real-estate developer who subsequently defaults on interest. Which risk TYPE in Section 7.2 is primarily being realised?

answer.text: Credit Risk (embedded in Debt Financing Risk per Section 7.1.1 / Investment Strategy Risk) — interest default and capital-recovery risk.
Operational Risk — system failure at the fund administrator.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 7.1.1(6) Debt Financing Related Risks: 'Debt financing is subject to credit risk which would consist mainly of interest rate risk and default risk… There could be risk in recovery of interest as well as capital in such investments arising from default, illiquidity and debt resolution process.' An interest default is the textbook credit-risk realisation. The Trap: Speculative (A) is for public-market directional strategies. Operational (C) is internal to the fund. Cyber (D) is unrelated. Note: The workbook identifies recovery risk for interest and capital due to default, illiquidity, and debt-resolution processes as part of the credit risk embedded in debt financing.
